steps.name: Distant Voice
steps.text: Hurry it up! You in the back, keep up!

steps.name: Distant Voice
steps.text: Our intel indicates that the target should be around here. Search carefully, and leave no stone unturned!
After that woman left the room, an unknown amount of time passed, to the point that time itself seemed alien to Monch.
Only the stinging pain of the ropes tightly binding her reminds her that she has not yet lost consciousness.
Finally, a hopeful sound comes from beyond the door, and Monch musters what might she has left to shout out.

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: I'm... over here...

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: I'm—
But try as she might, her parched throat can hardly produce a sound.
She laboriously crawls towards the door.
It opens.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Monch!

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Madam... Why are you here...?

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: We've been searching for you ever since the Catastrophe hit! That damned Silverash, pretentious bastard. Thought they actually had some useful intel... but in the end, I still ended up having to do all the legwork myself to find you!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: How're you doing? You hurt anywhere?

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Wait, your leg—

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: I'm... fine...

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: Madam, listen to me...

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: The researcher I'm tracking... She's from Victoria, but more important... she's got ties, to Columbia...

steps.name: Monch
steps.text: What they're really after is...

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Monch! MONCH!
Along the narrow mountain path, the convoy slowly plods onward.
After the incident's sudden outbreak, no shortage of people left their cars to observe the conflict's epicenter.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Turn off the engine. Get out.

steps.name: Victorian Agent
steps.text: What do you think you're doing? Who the hell are you people?

steps.name: Victorian Agent
steps.text: I... I'm an industrial investigator dispatched from Victoria! This is illegal obstruction of official business!

steps.name: Victorian Agent
steps.text: You've damaged our property, endangered Victorian lives, and almost even caused an accident! Mark my words, the Vine-Bead Court will hear of this!

steps.name: Victorian Agent
steps.text: Never should've come to this bloody shithole...

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: ...Are you done?

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Did you get all the pictures?

steps.name: Silverash Clan Guard
steps.text: Yessir!

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: This is no time for you to try to twist the narrative, Victorian. Just cooperate.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Open up the rear compartment.

steps.name: Matterhorn
steps.text: Unwilling to cooperate? Fine by me. You're more than welcome to conserve your energy to fend for yourselves before the court–if you're cold, I can offer you a blanket.
Matterhorn waves his hand, and the guard pries open the rear compartment without a word.
Seated upright upon a haystack there is an old cleric.
He brushes the dust off his body and walks out.
It is an emotionless affair, hardly amounting to courage.
The old cleric gazes upon the blinding brightness before him, and recollects the scenes from before.
Some ten minutes ago...

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Why'd the truck stop?

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Have we arrived?
Carolin lowers her voice.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: ...Did something happen?

steps.name: Elderly Cleric
steps.text: Stay calm, young lady.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: ...Did they find us?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: I didn't expect to find you here, Cleric of the Vine-Bead Court.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Let's continue this conversation elsewhere. This place is less than ideal.

steps.name: Elderly Cleric
steps.text: You are as hasty as always, young master of Clan Edelweiss.

steps.name: Elderly Cleric
steps.text: Honorable friends of Clan Silverash, I apologize for disturbing your work during this inclement weather.

steps.name: Elderly Cleric
steps.text: I am more than glad to go along with your arrangements.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Looks like the one we're after isn't here.

steps.name: Elderly Cleric
steps.text: I do believe this is where we part ways, young lady from Victoria.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Are you getting off?

steps.name: Elderly Cleric
steps.text: No, I'll stay here. Just keep walking forward, and don't look back.

steps.name: Elderly Cleric
steps.text: The entrance isn't far off. Silverash's people will surely notice this truck. Get out of here before they find you.

steps.name: Elderly Cleric
steps.text: By Kjeragandr... trust me.
The old cleric helps Carolin up.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: I'll do as you said.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: But, you'll also be exposed.

steps.name: Elderly Cleric
steps.text: That, too, is Kjeragandr's will. What I cannot change, I shall therefore accept.

steps.name: Elderly Cleric
steps.text: I ask only for Her forgiveness.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: I can't say I understand what your beliefs truly are—but maybe some day, I will.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: I respect your beliefs, so I will also try to find a way to live in peace. Best of luck to you, sir.
Carolin gets out of the truck and runs without stopping, in a direction leading far, far from Kjerag.
Shedding her stained cleric's robes, she shivers from the cold.
Alone she walks through the vast, pale mountainscape.
Until in the distance, a dark tunnel entrance beckons to her.
Through the telescope's lens, Gnosis sees the mysterious scientist step into the shadows.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Arrest these two and have them sent straight to the Vine-Bead Court.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: I've brought one.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I'm afraid I cannot grant your wish, Great Elder.
Upon hearing that long-awaited voice, Enciodes stands up and walks past the old man who remains frozen like a wooden sculpture.

steps.name: Degenbrecher
steps.text: Gnosis executed the plan. The Tschäggättä deployed immediately on his signal.
Before the presence of these wraiths, the clerics could do nothing but stumble back into their abodes, their tender faces affixed in fear.

steps.name: Vine-Bead Apprentice Cleric
steps.text: I, I'm one of the Vine-Bead Court's clerics! You can't treat me like this—

steps.name: Tschäggättä
steps.text: Shut up and stop resisting!

steps.name: Vine-Bead Apprentice Cleric
steps.text: ...Master Frey is here too! Please, help me!
The one just brought in was the once-arrogant envoy of the Vine-Bead Court. His gaze sweeps over the shouting cleric, and he shakes his head.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Father Frey, I believe I can now explain your actions.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Victoria's agents conspired with the Vine-Bead Court's clerics to smuggle spies out of the country through the mine railway, but were caught red-handed thanks to Karlan Trade.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: And before that, you were assisting the Victorians with scouring the mining site. Premeditated ill-intent.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: And lest you forget, you protected the suspect following Ratatos's funeral.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: You will formally be put on trial for these crimes.

steps.name: Vine-Bead Court Envoy
steps.text: By Kjeragandr... Forgive him, for he knows not of what he speaks––

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: It is a fact that spies have infiltrated the Vine-Bead Court. I urge you to not resist. Cooperation with our investigation is the only path to leniency.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Take Elder Great Adso, Father Frey, and the other elders of the Vine-Bead Court away for questioning. The other clerics are to remain there, awaiting their summons.

steps.name: Tschäggättä
steps.text: Yessir!

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Now then, Great Elder Adso––

steps.name: Adso
steps.text: Silverash, do you think you've won?

steps.name: Adso
steps.text: 'Those who live by the blade will find their arrogance short-lived.'

steps.name: Adso
steps.text: I wonder, just how long will your arbitrary reign of terror last?
Without making any unnecessary movements, Adso gives a slight nod to the crowd, then slowly walks to the door.

steps.name: Vine-Bead Apprentice Cleric
steps.text: Great Elder! What should we do?!

steps.name: Adso
steps.text: ...Survive.

steps.name: Adso
steps.text: The rest is already written in the scriptures. I have nothing else to say.

steps.name: Adso
steps.text: You are Her servants, and whatever happens, you must act according to your conscience.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Take him away.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: By Kjeragandr, may the guilty receive their fair trial.

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: This is an abandoned mining shaft—the torches and tunnel lights don't work anymore. Bend down carefully, and watch your head...

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: If we wrap around from this side, we should just be able to make it...

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: Urgh!

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Watch out!

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: ...Come over first. Watch your step.
Joanna shifts her feet, and several rocks tumble down the cave, the sounds of dislodged pebbles echoing through the cracked crevices as they fall. She shudders.

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: So deep... You'd probably turn into a stain on the ground if you fell from this height...

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: Damn those Victorians for causing trouble in the mines... Else, we wouldn't have to come this way...

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: Huh? Saintess, what are you looking at?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: There's a light ahead; it must be the path leading to the main ore vein. Come—let's hold hands, just like before.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: We are just a few steps shy of our answer. We mustn't run into danger here.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Soon... We will find all our answers.
The map is illuminated by the flickering light of the oil lamp. They hardly converse, moving forward in silence, their steps filled with both fear and anticipation.
But eventually, the search comes to an end.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: ...Are you sure this is the right place? Might we have made a mistake?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: No... I'm sure of it.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: This is the mine I previously calculated and located... There's no way this could be the wrong place.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: What are you two talking about? This is the place we were looking for, yeah?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: According to my plan, we should be able to find an Originium vein here... My deduction can be proven correct, if and only if it exists...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: But, this place...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: ...is an Oriron mine.

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: I've investigated and analyzed everything; these are all just ordinary Oriron deposits. There's no chance they're related to Catastrophe...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: ...Let alone any traces of 'extraterrestrial objects'. Where did we go wrong?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: But, why?! We clearly saw a bunch of trucks transporting Originium on our way here! How could this all just be Oriron?
It doesn't take long for Enya to grasp the schemes of the man bonded to her by blood.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Indeed... We came to the wrong place.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: The mineral vein here is not the 'Heart of Karlan', but rather, the 'Bones of Kjerag'...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: The bones that uphold Kjerag's spine...

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: ...Um, may I say something?

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: The Heart of Karlan is a pure core that validates faith. Man's eyes, ears, mouth, nose, and hands can deceive, and only the heart cannot. Such is written in the Kjeragandr.

spans.text: The Heart of Karlan is a pure core that validates faith. Man's eyes, ears, mouth, nose, and hands can deceive, and only the heart cannot. Such is written in the

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: But, I don't think we're being unfaithful or impious.

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: We all know how much we've done... and surely, She must know too.

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: Just like how give everything on the hunt, only to come up empty-handed and go hungry through the night.

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: But, we must have faith. Faith in the land of Kjerag. Faith in Kjeragandr's protection. She promised us that as long as we have our two hands, we shall not starve or freeze to death in Kjerag's lands.

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: So, Great Saintess, come. Let's try again––

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Huh? Try... what?

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: Use your bell to call Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: That sweet bell—the sound of the Saintess who played to awaken Kjeragandr, the clear sound beloved of Her, the sound that is Her call.

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: So it says in the Kjeragandr that burdenbeasts wearing this bell will not be snatched away by wild beasts; they shall not fall ill or die young, and shall find their way back home should they ever be lost.

spans.text: that burdenbeasts wearing this bell will not be snatched away by wild beasts; they shall not fall ill or die young, and shall find their way back home should they ever be lost.

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: For one's 'heart to be astray' is to be lost too, right? I don't totally get what it means, but I heard it from one of the clerics at the Vine-Bead Court!
Unlike her two dejected companions, the girl shows no signs of discouragement and is eager to try again.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: That's right. We should keep trying. Perhaps Kjeragandr will respond to us.
The silver bell rings out on high, its engraved patterns shimmering beneath the hazy light of the miner's lamps.
She had tried to call out like this before. At the Vine-Bead Court, in her own bedroom, among her books, while resting among the snow-capped mountains.
Ring—ring—
The clear, cold sound of the silver bell echoes through the empty cave.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: ...Woah, that's...!

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: This sound, this frequency... Why does it sound so alike?!

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Did you discover something?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: That frequency! The echoes of your bell throughout the cave sound just like that one audio recording from the observatory—almost identical, even!

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Is that just a coincidence?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: A coincidence? No...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: 'In nature, no two snowflakes are exactly alike'...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Say, Saintess... Where exactly did that bell come from?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: That would require going back to very ancient legends...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: In Kjerag history, there was a long span of time where Kjeragandr fell into deep slumber until She was awoken by a devout Saintess.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: It was Kjeragandr's gift to that Saintess.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I've also heard that when subsequent craftsmen made bells for the Saintesses, they sought to imitate the sounds of the mountains...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: The sounds of the mountains...? What kind of mountain could make a sound––

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: A Feranmut?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Impossible... How could that be...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Snap out of it, Elena... You're a scientist. How could you let your faith falter at a time like this...?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Elena, are you saying that on the day before the Catastrophe, something fell onto Mount Karlan, thus creating that sound?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Based on my previous conjectures, yes...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: So think about it this way... If we think of the mountain as a huge bell, doesn't that mean there's probably a huge hollow inside it?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Theoretically speaking, that would... be possible... But, do you know where a massive hollow like that could exist?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: There is a rumor not recorded in Kjerag's official history, and it also happens to be related to the Saintess who awakened Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: A long, long time ago, there once was an uprising against the Vine-Bead Court in Kjerag.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: The people had grown dissatisfied because Kjeragandr had not performed any miracles in a long time, and so they marched upon the Vine-Bead Court. Their wrath was only quelled when the Saintess awakened the sleeping deity.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: During the chaos, a number of clerics took their precious scriptures and took refuge within Mount Karlan, therefore preserving some of their valuable knowledge.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Yet regardless, the classic works of the Vine-Bead Court still suffered a break in continuity around that time.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: What if... the account of Kjeragandr leaving her people within the scriptures... is actually a description of this event?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Great Saintess... If this sanctuary truly exists, will we find traces of the 'Kjeragandr' there?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Where should we even look?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Behind the Vine-Bead Court... the place leading to Mount Karlan's summit.
Enya tightly grips the silver bell in her hand. She seems to hear the wind and the snow, as well as the footsteps that would occasionally shadow her while she worked at the Vine-Bead Court.
Whose voice was that? Who was calling to her from behind? Who would pat her on the shoulders and bring honeyed cystymilk to her while she was burning the midnight oil to organize her scriptures?
All she can hear and see is the pure white snow that never stops blowing with the wind.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: O Kjeragandr on high, please grant us your guidance.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: May the path we walk be true.
'A cleric from the Vine-Bead Court, in collusion with Victorian agents, stole important military intelligence and was arrested yesterday.'
'Great Elder Adso confessed to some of these allegations, and agreed to fully cooperate with the investigation. During this time, all activities of the Vine-Bead Court are to be suspended.'
'There is considerable evidence suggesting that Victorian agents are involved in a string of unusual natural and social phenomena.'
'Karlan Trade is also assembling scientific researchers to assess the possibility of an espionage-related Catastrophe.'
'As a reminder to all citizens of Kjerag: If any foreign national approaches you under the guise of offering charity, business ventures, or gathering news, please be extremely vigilant...'

steps.name: Angered Local
steps.text: I knew it!

steps.name: Angered Local
steps.text: The Great Elder and that Victorian duke are in cahoots! Look what those bastards have brought upon us!

steps.name: Anxious Local
steps.text: Couldn't it just be one big misunderstanding? If even the Vine-Bead Court has betrayed Kjeragandr... My goodness...

steps.name: Angered Local
steps.text: They've been mucking about with the Victorians, and you still give them the benefit of the doubt?

steps.name: Anxious Local
steps.text: But, hasn't the Karlan Trade you seem to trust so much been dealing with Victoria this whole time...?

steps.name: Angered Local
steps.text: The only reason you can even hear all this on the radio is thanks to Karlan Trade. But what about the Vine-Bead Court? What've they ever done for you?

steps.name: Nosy Local
steps.text: Stop your bickering. Victorian broadcasting has a response. Shut up and listen.

steps.name: Angered Local
steps.text: I don't give a damn what they have to say!

steps.name: Anxious Local
steps.text: ...I need to make sense of all of this.
'Sir Wilson, you are highly respected by Her Grace the Duke, as well as an expert on the Kjerag affair. We would like to ask you—how should we interpret the attitude displayed by Enciodes Silverash?
'I see it as nothing more than a way of quelling the public discontent in Kjerag. Enciodes has always been a close partner of Victoria.'
'Don't you find that somewhat difficult to believe?'
'Even based on publicly-available information, it is an indisputable fact that Victoria has been the primary beneficiary of many of the trade contracts strongly spearheaded by Enciodes himself.'

'With the help of Karlan Trade, Kjerag's development has almost entirely come off the back of Victoria's aid, from the import of breeding beasts and fertilizers to railway technology and even Originium processing.'
'In return, Enciodes has committed to handing over more than forty percent of Kjerag's natural resources for Victoria's development.'
'Not along ago, Karlan Trade also handed over a mining site that was being worked by Kazimierz to the Duke of Caster.'
'Then, it seems that Enciodes is trying to maintain an attitude of ambiguity. That being the case, are you not worried that his attempts to soothe the public will anger the Duke?'

'Lest you forget, Enciodes is the Duke's grand-nephew, and the blood of Caster flows in his veins. The delicate understanding between him and the Duke is, without a doubt, difficult for outsiders to grasp.'

'What you may not know is that even while he issued the statement, he also submitted a new mining agreement to the Duke, who has already signed and returned it. Expect a joint announcement on this matter in short time.'
'I have obtained the key points of this agreement and would like to share them with you here. Do take a look at these graphs, good sir.'
''Karlan Trade is willing to entrust 100% of future mining rights to a foundation established jointly with the Duke of Caster'. This truly is...'
'Just the tip of the iceberg. Look at what comes next...'

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: Nonsense!
The young reporter is startled by the volume of her outburst. She instinctively reaches to pat her bulging backpack before turning around.
Seeing the empty street makes her let out a heavy sigh.

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: Phew... Looks like they won't be able to catch up to me.

steps.name: Victorian Reporter
steps.text: Camera, recorder, film prints... Everything's here. This time, I won't let them take these away!
She then looks at the statue of Kjeragandr in the distance, pulls down the brim of her hat, and walks toward the city's center.
